designs.feature: Add current/selected track to a playlist
designs.summary: A new picker mode (MODE_ADD_TO_PLAYLIST) opened with the "y" key from player, queue, and browse modes. It lists the user's editable playlists (session.user.playlists() filtered to isinstance tidalapi.UserPlaylist), adds the target track via UserPlaylist.add() with server-side duplicate skipping, and shows a transient toast ("Added to X" / "Already in X") rendered by the existing 4fps loop. A "+ New playlist" row with inline name entry ships as a follow-up increment using session.user.create_playlist().
designs.approach:
## Data flow

**Target track resolution** — new helper `_target_track_for_picker()` on `HeadlessTidalPlayer`, resolved at the moment "y" is pressed:
- `MODE_PLAYER`: `self._current_track`
- `MODE_QUEUE`: `self._queue[self._queue_cursor]` (falls back to `_current_track` if queue empty)
- `MODE_BROWSE`: `self._browse_tracks[self._browse_cursor]` if `_browse_cursor >= 0`, else `_current_track`
- `MODE_SEARCH`: **excluded in v1** — printable keys append to `_search_query` (see `_handle_search_key`), so a letter binding can't work there without a chord. Returns `None` → no-op.

The resolved `tidalapi.Track` is stored in `self._picker_track` so later cursor movement in the originating view can't change what gets added.

**Picker open** — `_open_playlist_picker()`:
1. If `_target_track_for_picker()` is None, set toast "No track selected" and return.
2. `self._push_nav()` (existing nav-stack pattern captures the current mode's cursor/state), then `self._mode = self.MODE_ADD_TO_PLAYLIST`, `self._picker_cursor = 0`, `self._picker_message = ""`.
3. If `self._editable_playlists` cache is empty or older than 60s, set `self._picker_loading = True` and spawn a daemon thread (identical shape to `_load_playlists`):
   ```python
   pls = self.session.user.playlists()
   editable = [p for p in pls if isinstance(p, tidalapi.UserPlaylist)]
   self._editable_playlists = editable   # assign, never mutate in place
   ```
   The `isinstance` filter is the verified editability check: `Playlist.factory()` (tidalapi/playlist.py:152) only returns a `UserPlaylist` when `creator.id == session.user.id`; followed/editorial playlists stay plain `Playlist`. `users/{id}/playlists` already returns only user-created lists, so the filter is a safety net for edge cases (e.g. ARTIST-type lists).
   Note: `factory()` re-fetches each playlist (`Playlist.__init__` does a GET when given an id, to capture the `etag` header that `UserPlaylist.add` needs for `If-None-Match`). That N+1 cost is why the list is cached across picker opens and loaded off-thread.

**Selection / add** — `_picker_add_to(playlist)`:
- Guard `self._picker_busy` (set True before spawning, False in `finally`) so Enter key-repeat can't double-add.
- Daemon thread:
  ```python
  added = playlist.add([str(track.id)])          # onDupes=SKIP server-side
  if added: toast = f"Added to {playlist.name}"
  else:     toast = f"Already in {playlist.name}"
  playlist_name/num_tracks refresh is free: add() calls _reparse() internally
  ```
  On exception: toast "Failed to add — try again". No client-side duplicate pre-check needed; the returned `addedItemIds` (empty on skip) is authoritative.
- The picker closes immediately on Enter (`self._go_back()`), before the network call finishes; the toast appears in whatever mode the user returned to.

**Toast mechanism** — two new fields `self._toast: str = ""`, `self._toast_until: float = 0`. Setter `_set_toast(msg, seconds=2.5)` sets `self._toast_until = time.time() + seconds`. In `_build_display`, right after the player section (and also in the `_mini_player` branch), append `✓ {toast}` in `bold green` while `time.time() < self._toast_until`. The existing 4fps `live.update(self._build_display())` loop clears it with no timer thread. This toast is generic infrastructure — `_toggle_like` and `_remove_from_queue` can adopt it later.

## Mode system: new mode, not overlay

`MODE_ADD_TO_PLAYLIST = "add_to_playlist"` following the existing pattern exactly:
- Dispatch entry in `_handle_key` (after the `_quit_pending`/`_logout_pending` guards).
- `_handle_add_to_playlist_key(key)`: Up/Down move `_picker_cursor` over rows (row 0 = "+ New playlist…", rows 1..N = `_editable_playlists`); Enter/→ selects; Esc/← calls `_go_back()`; Space keeps the global play/pause behavior with the `_space_held` guard, copied from `_handle_playlists_key`.
- `_build_add_to_playlist_display()`: header `Add "{track.name}" to…`, PAGE_SIZE pagination copied from `_build_playlists_display`, showing `name` + `num_tracks` per row. Loading state renders "Loading playlists…"; empty state renders "No playlists yet — press Enter to create one".
- `_push_nav`/`_go_back`: add a `MODE_ADD_TO_PLAYLIST` branch to `_push_nav` (store cursor) — but the picker itself never pushes further nav, it only pops, so `_go_back` needs no new branch (popping restores the originating mode's saved state, which all existing branches already handle).
- Controls line in `_build_display`: `[Enter] add  [↑/↓] navigate  [n] new playlist  [←/Esc] cancel`.

## "Create new playlist" sub-state (increment 3)

Row 0 of the picker (or key "n" inside the picker) sets `self._picker_naming = True`, `self._picker_new_name = ""`. While naming:
- `_handle_add_to_playlist_key` routes printable chars into `_picker_new_name`, Backspace deletes, Esc cancels back to the list, Enter spawns a daemon thread:
  ```python
  pl = self.session.user.create_playlist(name, "")   # description required, pass ""
  pl.add([str(track.id)])
  self._editable_playlists = [pl] + self._editable_playlists
  toast: f"Created '{name}' and added track"
  ```
- Display: replaces the list with a text-entry line styled like `_build_search_display`'s query line (`Name: {typed}█`).

## Keybinding

"y" ("add to plaYlist") in `_handle_player_key`, `_handle_queue_key`, `_handle_browse_key`. Verified free in all three (player uses space/k/n/s/t/m/l/r/q/p/o/arrows/Esc — "y" only appears in the `_logout_pending` guard, which is handled before mode dispatch and consumes its key; queue uses x; browse uses a). Add `[y] playlist` to the `_show_more` controls block in player mode and to the queue/browse control lines.

## Threading & consistency

Matches the codebase's existing no-lock convention: daemon threads assign whole new objects to shared attributes (`self._editable_playlists = editable`, `self._toast = ...`), never mutate lists the render loop is iterating. `_picker_busy` and `_picker_loading` are plain bool flips (atomic under the GIL). `UserPlaylist.add`'s internal `_reparse()` GET also runs inside the worker thread, so the render loop never blocks.

## Persistence (increment 4, optional)

Add `"last_playlist_id"` to the `_save_state()` dict in `~/.config/ticli/player_state.json` (alongside `track_ids`, `queue_index`, `position`, `search_history`). On picker open, move the matching playlist to the top of `_editable_playlists` so repeat adds are one keystroke. Restore in `_restore_state()` with `data.get("last_playlist_id")`.

## Shipping order (each independently mergeable)

1. Toast infra + picker mode + "y" in player mode only, add-to-existing.
2. Extend "y" to queue and browse via `_target_track_for_picker()`.
3. "+ New playlist" naming sub-state.
4. `last_playlist_id` persistence + pin-to-top.

## Tests

Follow the existing lightweight style in `src/ticli/tests/`: instantiate `HeadlessTidalPlayer.__new__` (or with a stubbed session), set `_mode`/`_queue`/`_queue_cursor`, and assert `_target_track_for_picker()` resolution per mode; assert `_set_toast` expiry math; feed keys to `_handle_add_to_playlist_key` with a fake `_editable_playlists` list of objects exposing `.name`/`.num_tracks` and assert cursor clamping and that Enter calls a monkeypatched `_picker_add_to`. No network required.

risks: session.user.playlists() is N+1 HTTP requests: Playlist.factory() constructs UserPlaylist(session, id), whose __init__ re-fetches each playlist to capture the etag header. With many playlists the picker's first open is slow — mitigated by background load, a 'Loading playlists…' state, and caching _editable_playlists across opens (60s TTL).

UserPlaylist.add() sends If-None-Match with a stale cached etag; a 412 (playlist changed elsewhere) surfaces as an exception — caught and shown as 'Failed to add' toast, but a retry-after-_reparse could be added later.

No-lock threading convention: worker threads must assign fresh list objects, never mutate _editable_playlists in place while the render loop iterates it (same discipline the rest of player.py follows).
Key-repeat on Enter could fire multiple adds — guarded by _picker_busy flag; the server-side onDupes=SKIP is a second safety net.

pyproject pins tidalapi>=0.8.0 but APIs were verified against installed 0.8.11 (e.g. add() returning addedItemIds, create_playlist on LoggedInUser); consider bumping the floor to the oldest release actually verified.
Search mode is excluded from v1 because printable keys feed _search_query; users may expect 'y' to work on a highlighted search track and instead type 'y' into the query.
open_questions: Is 'y' the right key, or would '+' (mnemonic but shifted) feel better? 'a' is taken by play-all in browse mode, so consistency across modes requires avoiding it.
Should search mode get picker access in v2 via a control chord (e.g. Ctrl-Y) despite the text-entry conflict, or is player/queue/browse coverage enough?
On duplicate ('Already in X'), silently skip with the toast, or offer a follow-up 'press y again to add anyway' using allow_duplicates=True?
Picker sort order: API order (creation order) vs alphabetical vs last-used pinned to top (increment 4)?
designs.alternatives_rejected: Overlay flag pattern (like _quit_pending/_logout_pending) instead of a full mode — rejected because the picker needs cursor navigation, pagination, and a text-entry sub-state; overlay flags in _handle_key would duplicate the per-mode dispatch machinery that modes already provide. Reusing MODE_PLAYLISTS with a 'picking' boolean — rejected: it overloads Enter (open vs add), entangles nav-history semantics, and blocks incremental shipping. Client-side duplicate detection by fetching playlist.tracks() before adding — rejected: UserPlaylist.add() with onDupes=SKIP returns addedItemIds authoritatively in one request. session.user.favorites.add_playlist — rejected: that follows a playlist, it does not add tracks. playlist_and_favorite_playlists() as the picker source — rejected: it mixes in followed playlists that would then need filtering out anyway, and users/{id}/playlists already returns exactly the user-created set.

designs.feature: Caching and responsiveness layer (in-memory TTL cache, disk snapshots, stream-URL prefetch, optimistic UI)
designs.summary: Add a small internal module `src/ticli/utils/cache.py` (a thread-safe TTL cache plus credential_store-style JSON disk snapshot helpers under ~/.config/ticli/cache/) and wire it into the seven read-path call sites in player.py so re-opening albums/playlists/artists/searches renders instantly, with stale-while-revalidate refreshes for mutable data. Separately fix the two worst latency bugs found by reading: `track.get_url()` currently runs on the UI thread on every play/skip (prefetch next track's URL and move misses to a daemon thread), and `_restore_state` re-fetches every queued track over the network at each launch (hydrate lightweight Track objects from a disk snapshot instead — zero network at startup). Shippable in four independent phases.
designs.approach:
## Profile-by-reading: every network call site in player.py

| # | Site (method, ~line) | Call | Problem |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `_login` (~340) | `load_oauth_session` / `check_login` / `login_oauth` | One-time; not cacheable. |
| 2 | `_load_favorites` (~398) | `session.user.favorites.tracks(limit=999)` | Re-fetched every launch; heart icons blank until it lands. Disk-snapshot candidate. |
| 3 | `_restore_state._run` (~437) | `self.session.track(tid)` **in a loop** | Worst offender: one HTTP round trip per queued track, every launch, for metadata we already had last session. |
| 4 | `_play_track` (~460) | `track.get_url()` | **Runs on the main/UI thread** (key handlers call `_next_track` → `_play_queue_index` → `_play_track` synchronously). Every play/skip stalls the Rich Live render loop for a network round trip. |
| 5 | `_toggle_like` (~503) | `favorites.add_track/remove_track` | Heart flips only after the API returns → laggy. Make optimistic. |
| 6 | `_start_track_radio` (~520) | `track.get_track_radio(limit=25)` | Re-pressing `r` on the same track re-fetches. |
| 7 | `_do_search._run` (~1021) | `session.search(query, models=..., limit=8)` | Re-searching the same query re-fetches. (Back-nav is already instant — `_push_nav` snapshots `results` — so only forward re-entry needs the cache.) |
| 8 | `_open_album._run` (~1069) | `album.tracks()` | Re-opening the same album from search always re-fetches. Album contents are near-immutable → long TTL. |
| 9 | `_open_artist._run` (~1091) | `artist.get_top_tracks(limit=20)` | Same. |
| 10 | `_load_playlists._run` (~1125) | `session.user.playlists()` | Opposite problem: `_handle_player_key('p')` only calls it `if not self._playlists` → cached **forever** in-session, never refreshed. Needs stale-while-revalidate. |
| 11 | `_open_playlist._run` (~1148) | `playlist.tracks()` | Re-opening a playlist re-fetches; this is the main browse path, biggest UX win. |

## The module: `src/ticli/utils/cache.py` (~120 LOC, stdlib only)

```python
CACHE_DIR = Path.home() / ".config" / "ticli" / "cache"   # mode 0o700, files 0o600

class TTLCache:
    """Thread-safe in-memory TTL cache with LRU eviction."""
    def __init__(self, max_entries: int = 128): ...
    def get(self, key: str, allow_stale: bool = False) -> Optional[tuple[Any, bool]]:
        """Returns (value, is_fresh) or None. allow_stale=True returns expired
        entries with is_fresh=False — the stale-while-revalidate read."""
    def put(self, key: str, value: Any, ttl: float) -> None
    def invalidate(self, prefix: str) -> None   # prefix match, e.g. "playlist_tracks:"

# Disk snapshots — same style/error-handling as credential_store.py:
def disk_read(name: str) -> Optional[Any]        # json.loads, returns None on any error
def disk_write(name: str, payload: Any) -> None  # mkdir 0o700, chmod 0o600, log-and-swallow
```

Internally: `OrderedDict` + one `threading.Lock` (the lock is private to the module; the player's existing no-locks model is untouched — fetch threads still write plain attributes read by the render loop). Entries store `(value, fresh_until)`. Disk is **JSON-only, our own minimal dicts** — never pickled tidalapi objects, never stream URLs (they're signed and expire).

### Key/TTL table (module constants)

| Key | TTL | Disk? |
|---|---|---|
| `search:{query.lower()}` | 300 s | no (holds live tidalapi objects) |
| `album_tracks:{album.id}` | 24 h | no |
| `artist_top:{artist.id}` | 1 h | no |
| `playlist_tracks:{playlist.id}` | 600 s + SWR | no |
| `user_playlists` | 600 s + SWR | `playlists.json` (id/name/num_tracks/creator) |
| `radio:{track_id}` | 600 s | no |
| `url:{track_id}:{quality}` | 300 s | **never** (signed URL) |
| liked track IDs | n/a (SWR on launch) | `liked_ids.json` |
| queue metadata | n/a | `queue_tracks.json` |

## Phase 1 — in-memory cache on the browse read paths (ship first)

`HeadlessTidalPlayer.__init__` gains `self._cache = TTLCache()` and `self._browse_gen = 0`. Each of `_open_album`, `_open_artist`, `_open_playlist`, `_do_search`, `_start_track_radio` gets the same 6-line pattern:

```python
def _open_playlist(self, playlist):
    self._push_nav(); self._mode = self.MODE_BROWSE; ...
    key = f"playlist_tracks:{playlist.id}"
    hit = self._cache.get(key, allow_stale=True)
    if hit:
        self._browse_tracks, fresh = hit[0], hit[1]
        self._browse_loading = False
        if fresh:
            return                      # instant, zero network
        # stale: already rendered; fall through to revalidate silently
    self._browse_gen += 1
    gen = self._browse_gen
    def _run():
        tracks = list(playlist.tracks())
        self._cache.put(key, tracks, ttl=600)
        if gen == self._browse_gen:     # a newer view hasn't superseded us
            self._browse_tracks = tracks
            self._browse_loading = False
    threading.Thread(target=_run, daemon=True).start()
```

The `_browse_gen` guard fixes a latent race the cache makes likelier: today, opening album A, pressing back, and opening album B can let A's slow thread clobber B's `_browse_tracks`. Same guard (a `_search_gen`) goes into `_do_search`.

`_load_playlists` keeps its `if not self._playlists` call-site guard removed; instead it always runs with SWR: serve `user_playlists` from cache instantly (or from `playlists.json` on cold start, rendered as name/num_tracks rows), then revalidate in background — fixing both the forever-stale list and the reload delay.

`_go_back` needs no changes — instant back already works via `_nav_history` snapshots; the cache adds instant *forward re-entry*.

## Phase 2 — stream-URL prefetch + un-block the UI thread

Verified: `Track.get_url()` (tidalapi/media.py:410) only needs `self.id` + session — it hits `tracks/{id}/urlpostpaywall` and returns `json["urls"][0]`.

- New `_prefetch_next_url()`: after `_play_track` succeeds, spawn a daemon thread that calls `self._queue[self._queue_index + 1].get_url()` and puts it under `url:{id}:{quality}` (ttl 300 s). Pressing → then plays with **zero network on any thread**.
- Rework `_play_track(track)`: check `url:` cache; on hit call `self.audio.play_url(url)` immediately. On miss, set `self._current_track = track` optimistically (title/artist render instantly — this is the perceived-responsiveness win), bump a `self._play_gen` counter, and fetch `get_url()` on a daemon thread; the thread only calls `play_url` if its gen still matches, so mashing next-next-next skips intermediates instead of playing each briefly. This removes the UI-thread network stall entirely.
- ffplay interplay: none needed — `AudioPlayer.play_url` already handles its own ffmpeg cache file per track; we only hand it the URL sooner.
- Optional (defer): first-page-fast loading for huge playlists using the verified `offset=` params — `playlist.tracks(limit=100, offset=0)` renders immediately, a background loop appends subsequent offsets to `_browse_tracks` (render loop tolerates growth; pagination math in `_build_browse_display` is already length-based).

## Phase 3 — optimistic like + favorites snapshot

- `_toggle_like`: mutate `self._liked_ids` **before** spawning the thread (heart flips at the next 250 ms frame); on API exception the thread reverts the set. Also `disk_write("liked_ids.json", sorted(self._liked_ids))` on success.
- `_load_favorites`: `disk_read("liked_ids.json")` synchronously (instant hearts at launch), then the existing background `favorites.tracks(limit=999)` revalidates and rewrites the snapshot.

## Phase 4 — instant queue restore (zero-network startup)

- `_save_state`: additionally `disk_write("queue_tracks.json", [{"id": t.id, "name": t.name, "duration": t.duration, "artist": (t.artists[0].name if t.artists else ""), "album": (t.album.name if t.album else "")} for t in self._queue])`. Keeps `player_state.json` schema untouched (ids remain the source of truth / fallback).
- `_restore_state`: if the snapshot's ids match `track_ids`, hydrate **without any network**. Verified against tidalapi source: `Media.__init__` (media.py:216) and `Artist.__init__`/`Album.__init__` skip their `_get` fetch when id is None, so:
  ```python
  t = tidalapi.media.Track(session=self.session)      # no fetch
  t.id, t.name, t.duration = m["id"], m["name"], m["duration"]
  a = tidalapi.artist.Artist(self.session, None); a.name = m["artist"]; t.artists = [a]; t.artist = a
  t.album = tidalapi.album.Album(self.session, None); t.album.name = m["album"]
  ```
  These are *real* session-bound Tracks: `get_url()`, `get_track_radio()`, `_toggle_like` all work (they use only `t.id` + session). All display builders already access only name/artists[0].name/duration/album.name. The old per-id `session.track(tid)` loop remains only as fallback for ids missing from the snapshot. Startup queue restore drops from N round trips to zero.

## Persistence & threading summary
- Disk: `~/.config/ticli/cache/{playlists,liked_ids,queue_tracks}.json`, dir 0o700 / files 0o600, all writes log-and-swallow — exactly the credential_store pattern.
- Threading model unchanged: daemon threads write attributes the 4 fps render loop reads; the only lock lives inside TTLCache; gen counters replace ordering guarantees.
- No keybinding or display-builder changes except `_load_playlists` losing its call-site guard; loading states appear only on true cache misses.

key_changes.change: NEW (~120 LOC, stdlib only): TTLCache class (OrderedDict + Lock, get(allow_stale=), put(ttl=), invalidate(prefix)), CACHE_DIR constant, disk_read/disk_write JSON snapshot helpers mirroring credential_store.py error handling and 0700/0600 permissions, and the key/TTL constants table.
__init__: add self._cache = TTLCache(), self._browse_gen / self._search_gen / self._play_gen counters.

_open_album, _open_artist, _open_playlist, _start_track_radio, _do_search: cache-first with allow_stale (stale-while-revalidate), gen-counter guard so slow threads can't clobber a newer view; loading state only on true miss.
_load_playlists + _handle_player_key('p'): remove the if-not-self._playlists guard; always SWR through 'user_playlists' key with cold-start render from cache/playlists.json snapshot.

_play_track: consult url:{id}:{quality} cache; on miss set _current_track optimistically and fetch get_url() on a daemon thread gated by _play_gen (removes the UI-thread network stall on every play/skip). New _prefetch_next_url() called after playback starts to warm the next queue track's URL.

_toggle_like: mutate _liked_ids before spawning the thread (optimistic heart), revert on API failure; persist liked_ids.json snapshot. _load_favorites: read snapshot synchronously for instant hearts, revalidate in background as today.

_save_state/_restore_state: write cache/queue_tracks.json metadata snapshot; restore by hydrating no-fetch Track/Artist/Album objects (verified id=None constructors skip network) instead of N session.track(tid) round trips; keep per-id fetch as fallback.
Unit tests for TTLCache (fresh/stale/evict/invalidate) and disk_read/disk_write round-trip with a tmp CACHE_DIR — pure stdlib, no TIDAL session needed, fits the existing no-network test style.

risks: Signed stream URLs expire server-side on an unknown schedule; the 300 s TTL for url:* keys is a guess. Mitigate: on ffplay exiting immediately (<2 s) after starting a prefetched URL, invalidate the key and refetch once.

Serving stale playlist tracks means edits made in the TIDAL app can be invisible for up to the TTL; SWR bounds this to one view-open, but the refresh silently swapping _browse_tracks under the cursor could shift the selected row — clamp _browse_cursor when the revalidated list is shorter.

Caching live tidalapi objects (Track lists) in memory keeps them bound to the session; harmless today, but after a token refresh the objects keep working since they hold a session reference, not tokens — verified Track only stores session/requests.

Hydrated Tracks from queue_tracks.json skip attributes we don't snapshot (e.g. explicit, popularity); any future display code touching those must use getattr guards like _build_queue_display already does.

Gen-counter guards fix the view-clobber race but state writes are still unlocked cross-thread; acceptable given GIL-atomic attribute assignment and the existing design, but worth noting in the module docstring.
Disk snapshots reveal listening data in plaintext; kept at 0600 in a 0700 dir, and no tokens/URLs are ever written.

Half-blocks are the only rendering path that coexists with a Rich Live region redrawn at 4fps and that works in Terminal.app (which supports no image protocol at all); escape-protocol images (iTerm2 OSC 1337, kitty, sixel) are explicitly rejected for the Live view. Cover URLs come from the verified `track.album.image(320)` tidalapi call, fetched on a daemon thread with an in-memory cache, matching the app's existing lock-free thread pattern.
designs.approach:
## Research conclusion: renderable vs escape-protocol images

**Recommendation: half-block Rich renderable. Do not ship protocol images in v1.**

The four options evaluated:

| Option | Works in Live? | iTerm2 | Terminal.app | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iTerm2 OSC 1337 (`ESC ] 1337 ; File=inline=1:...`) | No | Yes | No | Rejected |
| kitty graphics protocol (APC `_G`) | No | No (kitty/WezTerm/Ghostty only) | No | Rejected |
| sixel | No | Yes (3.3+) | No | Rejected |
| Half-block Unicode ("▀" + fg/bg ANSI colors) | **Yes** | Yes | Yes (256-color) | **Chosen** |

Why protocol images fight Rich Live: Live with `screen=False` (what ticli uses) repaints by cursor-moving up and re-emitting styled lines 4x/sec. Rich measures every renderable in *cells* and its Segment pipeline strips/mangles raw control sequences, so an escape-placed raster (a) isn't part of the cell grid Live tracks — each 250ms repaint overwrites or misaligns it, (b) would need its base64 payload (tens of KB) re-emitted every frame, flooding the tty, and (c) Terminal.app — a stated likely target — renders the escape as garbage or nothing. Half-blocks are ordinary styled Text: Live diffs and repaints them like any other content, and Rich auto-downgrades truecolor styles to 256-color on Apple_Terminal (it checks `COLORTERM`/`TERM_PROGRAM`), so Terminal.app gets a slightly banded but recognizable cover for free.

Detection still exists, but its v1 job is capability gating, not protocol selection: a `detect_art_backend()` function returns `"halfblock"` if Pillow imports and stdout is a tty, else `"none"`. It also records (for logging and a future high-res path) what the terminal *would* support via env sniffing: `TERM_PROGRAM == "iTerm.app"` / `"WezTerm"` → iTerm2 protocol capable; `TERM == "xterm-kitty"` or `KITTY_WINDOW_ID` set → kitty protocol; `TERM_PROGRAM == "Apple_Terminal"` → none. A future feature (e.g. "press `I` to splash full-res art while Live is paused") can consume this; the hook is designed but deliberately not built.

## Verified data source (tidalapi 0.8.11, installed at ~/.local/pipx/venvs/tidal-cli/)

- `Track.album` is `Optional[Album]` (media.py:208), populated during parse for search results, album/playlist tracks, and `session.track(id)` restores (media.py:247-249).
- `Album.image(dimensions=320)` → URL string; valid dims 80/160/320/640/1280/"origin" (album.py:243-279). Template: `https://resources.tidal.com/images/%s/%ix%i.jpg` (session.py:117). If `album.cover` is None it returns a TIDAL placeholder image URL (`DEFAULT_ALBUM_IMG`), so the call never needs a cover-missing branch — but guard `track.album is None`.
- `Album.cover` is the UUID cache key (set in `Album.parse`, album.py:116) — use it to key the render cache and to detect stale fetches.

Use 320px source (~30-60KB JPEG); fetch with stdlib `urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=10)` — no new HTTP dependency.

## New module: `src/ticli/utils/artwork.py` (mirrors credential_store.py style: module-level try/except import guard, small functions, logger)

```python
try:
    from PIL import Image
    ARTWORK_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    ARTWORK_AVAILABLE = False

ART_WIDTH = 24  # cells; renders 24x24 px over 12 terminal rows

def detect_art_backend() -> str: ...   # "halfblock" | "none" (+ logs protocol capability)

def render_cover(image_bytes: bytes, width: int = ART_WIDTH) -> Text:
    img = Image.open(io.BytesIO(image_bytes)).convert("RGB")
    img = img.resize((width, width), Image.LANCZOS)   # W px wide, W px tall
    # rows = width // 2; each row consumes 2 pixel-rows via "▀"
    for y in range(0, width, 2):
        for x in range(width):
            top, bot = img.getpixel((x, y)), img.getpixel((x, y + 1))
            text.append("▀", Style(color=Color.from_rgb(*top), bgcolor=Color.from_rgb(*bot)))
        text.append("\n")
```

Geometry: terminal cells are ~1:2 (w:h), half-blocks pack 2 pixels vertically per cell, so a W×W pixel image over W cells × W/2 rows displays square with zero distortion. 24 cells wide × 12 rows fits comfortably next to the 50-char progress bar (total ~80 cols). ~35 lines, Pillow-only; the render is done once per cover and cached as a `rich.text.Text`, so the 4fps loop pays nothing.

## Player wiring (`src/ticli/player.py`)

**State** (`__init__`): `self._show_artwork: bool = True`, `self._artwork_text: Optional[Text] = None`, `self._artwork_cover_id: Optional[str] = None`, `self._artwork_cache: OrderedDict[str, Text]` (LRU, cap 30).

**Fetch** — new `_request_artwork(self, track)`, same daemon-thread shape as `_toggle_like`/`_load_favorites`:
```python
def _request_artwork(self, track):
    if not (self._show_artwork and ARTWORK_AVAILABLE and track and track.album):
        return
    cover_id = track.album.cover or "default"
    if cover_id in self._artwork_cache:
        self._artwork_text = self._artwork_cache[cover_id]
        self._artwork_cover_id = cover_id
        return
    url = track.album.image(320)
    def _run():
        try:
            data = urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=10).read()
            text = render_cover(data)
            self._artwork_cache[cover_id] = text          # evict oldest past 30
            if self._current_track and self._current_track.album \
               and (self._current_track.album.cover or "default") == cover_id:
                self._artwork_cover_id = cover_id
                self._artwork_text = text                  # assign renderable LAST
        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug("Artwork fetch failed: %s", e)
    threading.Thread(target=_run, daemon=True).start()
```
Thread-safety follows the app's existing lock-free convention: the render loop only reads whole-object attributes; `_artwork_text` is assigned last so a torn state is never visible; the cover-id comparison at store time discards stale fetches when the user skips tracks quickly. Call sites: end of `_play_track` (covers manual play, queue advance, radio — everything routes through it) and inside `_restore_state`'s `_run` after `self._current_track = tracks[idx]`.

**Render** — leave `_build_player_display` untouched; compose in `_build_display`. Art shows only in full MODE_PLAYER view (never mini, never search/browse/queue/playlists — those need the vertical space):
```python
art_visible = (self._show_artwork and not self._mini_player
               and self._mode == self.MODE_PLAYER
               and self._artwork_text is not None
               and self._current_track is not None
               and self._current_track.album is not None
               and (self._current_track.album.cover or "default") == self._artwork_cover_id)
```
Step 1 (shippable alone): stack — `content.append_text(self._artwork_text)` before the player text; everything stays a single `Text`, zero layout risk. Step 2 (polish): side-by-side via `body = Table.grid(padding=(0, 2)); body.add_row(self._artwork_text, content); return Panel(body, ...)` — `Panel` accepts any renderable and `Table.grid` of Texts is fully Live-compatible.

**Toggle** — in `_handle_player_key`: `elif key == "c": ` → if `not ARTWORK_AVAILABLE`, set a transient status string ("Artwork requires Pillow: pip install 'tidal-cli[artwork]'") rendered in the status line; else flip `self._show_artwork`, and if turning on with a current track call `_request_artwork(self._current_track)`, then call `_save_state()` so the preference sticks even if the process later dies. Add `[c] cover` to the `_show_more` controls block in `_build_display` (next to `[l] like`).

**Persistence** — extend the existing player_state.json (not a new file): `_save_state` adds `"show_artwork": self._show_artwork`; `_restore_state` reads `self._show_artwork = data.get("show_artwork", True)` before the thread spawn. File already chmod-600 under ~/.config/ticli/.

## Packaging (`src/pyproject.toml`)

```toml
[project.optional-dependencies]
keyring = ["keyring>=24.0"]
artwork = ["Pillow>=10.0"]
```
Import-guarded exactly like keyring. Default `_show_artwork=True` is safe: without Pillow, `ARTWORK_AVAILABLE` is False and nothing renders or fetches.

## Tests (`src/ticli/tests/`)

`test_artwork.py`: `pytest.importorskip("PIL")`; build a 2x2 red/blue PIL image in-memory, encode to PNG bytes, assert `render_cover(data, width=4)` returns a Text with 2 lines of 4 "▀" chars and expected fg/bg styles; assert `detect_art_backend()` returns "none" when Pillow import is monkeypatched away. State round-trip test: write a player_state.json with `"show_artwork": false`, instantiate player, call `_restore_state`, assert flag. No network, fits the existing no-TIDAL-needed test philosophy.

## Ship plan (incremental)

1. **PR 1 (small):** `utils/artwork.py` + tests + `[artwork]` extra. No UI change.
2. **PR 2 (small):** fetch/cache wiring, `c` toggle, stacked art in player view, persistence.
3. **PR 3 (optional polish):** side-by-side `Table.grid` layout; optional disk cache at ~/.cache/ticli/art/{cover_id}-320.jpg; optional art-size cycling.

designs.summary: Spawn a tiny Python helper subprocess (part of the ticli package, run as `sys.executable -m ticli.utils.mac_media_helper`) whose main thread pumps an NSRunLoop and owns MPNowPlayingInfoCenter + MPRemoteCommandCenter via pyobjc; it talks to the player over JSON-lines on stdin/stdout. This was verified end-to-end on Garrett's machine (macOS 26.5.2): a non-bundled Python CLI process becomes the system Now Playing app and receives toggle/next/prev/pause/seek commands — but only when the run loop owns the process main thread, which is exactly why it must be a subprocess rather than a thread inside ticli. Shipped as an optional `media` pip extra gated to darwin; if pyobjc is missing or the helper fails, ticli behaves exactly as today.
designs.approach:
## Why a subprocess (empirically settled)

Two experiments run on this machine (macOS 26.5.2, pyobjc-framework-MediaPlayer from PyPI, verified with the `media-control` reader tool):

- **Main-thread run loop, plain CLI process (no app bundle, no NSApplication): WORKS.** The process became the system Now Playing app (`media-control get` showed our title/artist/album/duration, `processIdentifier` = the Python pid) and all of `toggle-play-pause`, `next-track`, `previous-track`, `pause`, and `seek` were delivered into Python handlers registered with `addTargetWithHandler_`.
- **Secondary-thread run loop while the main thread is busy (ticli's exact shape): SILENTLY FAILS.** No error is raised, but the system never registers the process and no commands arrive.

ticli's main thread runs the tty cbreak `_read_key` loop and cannot pump a run loop. Therefore the MediaPlayer machinery lives in a **helper subprocess** whose main thread does nothing but pump `NSRunLoop.runMode_beforeDate_` in 0.25s slices and poll stdin — the same slice-pumping loop I validated. This also isolates pyobjc crashes from the player and gives clean fallback semantics (helper dies → feature off, player unaffected).

## Components

### 1. `src/ticli/utils/mac_media_helper.py` (new, ~120 LOC, helper process entry)

Runs only as `python -m ticli.utils.mac_media_helper`. Top of module: `import MediaPlayer` / `from Foundation import NSRunLoop, NSDate` inside try/except → exit code 3 on ImportError (parent treats as "unavailable"). All API names below were executed successfully in the verification scripts:

- `MediaPlayer.MPNowPlayingInfoCenter.defaultCenter()`, `.setNowPlayingInfo_(dict)`, `.setPlaybackState_()` with `MPNowPlayingPlaybackStatePlaying` / `MPNowPlayingPlaybackStatePaused` / `MPNowPlayingPlaybackStateStopped`
- Info-dict keys: `MPMediaItemPropertyTitle`, `MPMediaItemPropertyArtist`, `MPMediaItemPropertyAlbumTitle`, `MPMediaItemPropertyPlaybackDuration`, `MPNowPlayingInfoPropertyElapsedPlaybackTime`, `MPNowPlayingInfoPropertyPlaybackRate`
- `MediaPlayer.MPRemoteCommandCenter.sharedCommandCenter()` with `playCommand()`, `pauseCommand()`, `togglePlayPauseCommand()`, `nextTrackCommand()`, `previousTrackCommand()`; each `.addTargetWithHandler_(handler)` where the handler returns `MPRemoteCommandHandlerStatusSuccess`. `changePlaybackPositionCommand().setEnabled_(False)` in Phase 1 so the Control Center scrubber isn't draggable-then-snapping (enable in Phase 3).
- Phase 2 artwork: `MPMediaItemArtwork.alloc().initWithBoundsSize_requestHandler_(size, lambda s: img)` with `AppKit.NSImage.alloc().initWithData_(nsdata)` (both bindings verified importable; AppKit comes free as a pyobjc-framework-MediaPlayer dependency).

**Main loop** (single-threaded): loop `rl.runMode_beforeDate_("kCFRunLoopDefaultMode", NSDate.dateWithTimeIntervalSinceNow_(0.25))`, then `select.select([sys.stdin], [], [], 0)` and read any pending JSON line. **stdin EOF → exit** (this is the orphan-prevention: if ticli crashes, the pipe closes and the helper exits, releasing the Now Playing slot).

**Protocol (JSON lines):**
- parent → helper: `{"cmd":"metadata","title":…,"artist":…,"album":…,"duration":240}` · `{"cmd":"state","playing":true,"position":12.3}` · `{"cmd":"artwork","b64":…}` (Phase 2) · `{"cmd":"quit"}`
- helper → parent: `{"event":"ready"}` after registration · `{"event":"command","name":"toggle"|"play"|"pause"|"next"|"prev"}` · `{"event":"seek","position":42.0}` (Phase 3)

Position is pushed only on transitions (play/pause/track-change/seek): macOS extrapolates elapsed time from `ElapsedPlaybackTime` + `PlaybackRate` + the timestamp of the last `setNowPlayingInfo_`, so no per-second updates are needed (confirmed: `media-control get` showed correct extrapolated elapsed time).

### 2. `src/ticli/utils/media_remote.py` (new, ~110 LOC, parent-side controller)

Follows `credential_store.py` style: module-level availability probe, everything wrapped so failure is a no-op + `logger.debug`.

```python
class MediaRemote:
    @staticmethod
    def available() -> bool:   # sys.platform == "darwin" and importlib.util.find_spec("MediaPlayer")
    def start(self, on_command) -> bool   # Popen + wait for "ready" (5s), spawn reader thread
    def update_metadata(self, title, artist, album, duration): ...
    def update_state(self, playing: bool, position: float): ...
    def stop(self): ...        # send quit, close stdin, terminate after 2s
```

- Spawns `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-m", "ticli.utils.mac_media_helper"], stdin=PIPE, stdout=PIPE, stderr=DEVNULL, text=True)` — `sys.executable` inside the pipx venv guarantees the same interpreter/site-packages.
- A **daemon reader thread** (matching the codebase's existing daemon-thread convention) reads stdout lines and calls `on_command(name, **kwargs)`. EOF or JSON error → sets `self._alive = False`, feature degrades silently; no auto-restart in v1.
- All writes go through one `_send(dict)` that catches `BrokenPipeError`/`OSError` and flips `_alive` — after that every public method is a no-op.

**Fallback chain:** not darwin → off; `find_spec("MediaPlayer")` None (extra not installed) → off; helper exits code 3 or no `ready` in 5s → terminate + off; helper dies mid-session → off until next launch. In every case ticli behaves exactly as today.

### 3. Hooks in `src/ticli/player.py` (~40 LOC delta)

- `HeadlessTidalPlayer.__init__`: `self._media = None`.
- `run()`: after `self._login()` succeeds, `if MediaRemote.available(): self._media = MediaRemote(); self._media.start(self._on_media_command)`. In the existing `finally:` block (alongside `_save_state()` / `audio.stop()`): `if self._media: self._media.stop()`.
- `_play_track()`: after `self._playing = True`, call new `self._push_media_metadata(track)` → `update_metadata(track.name, ", ".join(a.name for a in track.artists), track.album.name if track.album else "", track.duration)` + `update_state(True, 0.0)`. Also covers `_next_track`/`_prev_track`/`_play_queue_index`/auto-advance since they all funnel through `_play_track`.
- `_toggle_play()`: at end, `if self._media: self._media.update_state(self._playing, self._get_position())`.
- `_monitor_playback()`: in the queue-exhausted branch (`self._playing = False`), also push `update_state(False, position)`.
- New `_on_media_command(name, **kw)` (called on the reader thread — same lock-free shared-state mutation pattern the existing daemon threads use):
  - `"toggle"` → `self._toggle_play()`
  - `"play"` → `if not self._playing: self._toggle_play()`
  - `"pause"` → `if self._playing: self._toggle_play()`
  - `"next"` → `self._next_track()`; `"prev"` → `self._prev_track()`

```toml

keyring = ["keyring>=24.0"]
media = ["pyobjc-framework-MediaPlayer>=10.3; sys_platform == 'darwin'"]
```

designs.feature: Search improvements: infinite scroll, type filters, and my-playlists search
designs.summary: Extend MODE_SEARCH with a filter row cycled by Tab/Shift-Tab (ALL / TRACKS / ALBUMS / ARTISTS / PLAYLISTS / MY PLAYLISTS). Single-type filters use tidalapi's verified `Session.search(query, models=..., limit, offset)` pagination so pressing Down at the last row appends the next page (up to TIDAL's 300-item search cap). MY PLAYLISTS searches a client-side JSON index of the user's playlist tracks (built in background, incrementally refreshed via each playlist's `last_updated`/`num_tracks`), since TIDAL has no server-side playlist-content search.
designs.approach:
## Verified tidalapi facts this design rests on (tidalapi 0.8.11, installed source)

- `Session.search(query, models=None, limit=50, offset=0)` (`session.py:771`) sends `limit`/`offset`/`types` as query params to the `search` endpoint. The docstring states the 300-item cap: "there aren't more than 300 items available in a search." **`offset` applies to every requested type simultaneously** (one request, one offset param), so clean pagination only works when `models` contains a single type. Result dict keys: `"tracks"`, `"albums"`, `"artists"`, `"videos"`, `"playlists"`, `"top_hit"` — playlists ARE a searchable type (`SearchTypes` at `session.py:61` includes `playlist.Playlist`).
- `Playlist.tracks(limit=None, offset=0, ...)` (`playlist.py:201`) — paginated track fetch per playlist.
- `Playlist` attributes: `id`, `name`, `num_tracks` (`playlist.py:54`), `last_updated: Optional[datetime]` (`playlist.py:59`, may be None).
- `LoggedInUser.playlists()` (`user.py:153`) — user's own playlists, not paginated. `LoggedInUser.playlist_and_favorite_playlists(offset, limit=50)` (`user.py:191`) — own + favorited, paginated at 50.
- `session.playlist(playlist_id)` (`session.py:838`) and `session.track(id)` (already used in `_restore_state`) — reconstruct objects from cached IDs.
- **No server-side playlist-content search exists** anywhere in tidalapi — hence the client-side index for feature 3.

## 1. Search type filter (build first — the other two hang off it)

New module constants in `player.py` next to the KEY_* block:

```python
KEY_TAB = "\t"            # not printable → never collides with query typing
KEY_SHIFT_TAB = "\x1b[Z"  # _read_key already slurps up to 7 bytes after ESC
KEY_CTRL_R = "\x12"
SEARCH_FILTERS = ["all", "tracks", "albums", "artists", "playlists", "mine"]
SEARCH_PAGE = 25
SEARCH_MAX = 300  # TIDAL search cap per tidalapi docstring
```

**Key collision audit of `_handle_search_key`** (why Tab/Shift-Tab/Ctrl-R are the only safe choices): taken keys are ESC, ←, →, ↑, ↓, Enter (\r,\n), Space (play/pause), Backspace (\x7f,\x08), and *every* printable char appends to `_search_query`. So no letter key can be a filter hotkey; Tab (`"\t".isprintable()` is False), Shift-Tab, and Ctrl-R fall through today's handler unhandled. Elsewhere: player-mode keys (space,k,n,s,t,m,l,r,q,p,o), browse `a`, queue `x` — none conflict since they're other modes.

New `__init__` state: `_search_filter = "all"`, `_search_offset = 0`, `_search_has_more = False`, `_search_loading_more = False`, `_search_gen = 0` (generation counter — every worker thread captures `gen = self._search_gen` and bails before mutating shared state if it changed; this replaces locks for the append-heavy flows below).

Handler additions in `_handle_search_key` (before the printable-char branch):

```python
elif key in (KEY_TAB, KEY_SHIFT_TAB):
    self._cycle_search_filter(+1 if key == KEY_TAB else -1)
elif key == KEY_CTRL_R and self._search_filter == "mine":
    self._rebuild_playlist_index(force=True)
```

`_cycle_search_filter(delta)` rotates `SEARCH_FILTERS`, bumps `_search_gen`, resets `_search_results/_search_cursor/_search_offset/_search_message`, and re-runs `_do_search()` if `_search_query.strip()` — so Tab on an existing query instantly re-slices it.

`_do_search` branches on `_search_filter`:
- `"all"`: today's behavior, plus playlists — `session.search(q, models=[tidalapi.Track, tidalapi.Album, tidalapi.Artist, tidalapi.Playlist], limit=8)`, slices 5 tracks / 3 albums / 2 artists / 2 playlists. No infinite scroll here (offset is per-type-simultaneous; a mixed page-2 would be incoherent). Footer hints "Tab: filter by type for more".
- single type: `session.search(q, models=[MODEL], limit=SEARCH_PAGE, offset=0)`; results from the matching key; `_search_offset = SEARCH_PAGE`; `_search_has_more = len(batch) == SEARCH_PAGE`.
- `"mine"`: pure in-memory index search (section 3) — runs synchronously, no thread.

Playlist results are `{"type": "playlist", "name": pl.name, "artist": creator-name-or-"", "obj": pl}`; `_select_search_result` gets a `"playlist"` branch calling the existing `_open_playlist(obj)` (which already does `_push_nav` → MODE_BROWSE). `type_styles` in `_build_search_display` gains `"playlist": "bold blue"` and `"mytrack": "bold cyan"`.

`_build_search_display` renders a filter bar under the query line — `ALL · TRACKS · ALBUMS · ARTISTS · PLAYLISTS · MY PLAYLISTS`, active one `bold reverse`, others `dim`. `_push_nav`/`_go_back` MODE_SEARCH dicts gain `"filter"`, `"offset"`, `"has_more"` keys so ←/Esc from an opened album restores the exact filtered page. The MODE_SEARCH controls line in `_build_display` gains `[Tab] filter`.

## 2. Infinite scroll (single-type filters only)

In `_handle_search_key`, the KEY_DOWN branch becomes:

```python
elif key == KEY_DOWN:
    if self._search_results:
        at_bottom = self._search_cursor >= len(self._search_results) - 1
        self._search_cursor = min(len(self._search_results) - 1, self._search_cursor + 1)
        if at_bottom:
            self._maybe_load_more()
```

`_maybe_load_more()` no-ops unless `_search_filter in ("tracks","albums","artists","playlists")`, `_search_has_more`, not `_search_loading_more`, and `_search_offset < SEARCH_MAX`. Otherwise it sets `_search_loading_more = True` and spawns a daemon thread:

```python
def _run(gen=self._search_gen, offset=self._search_offset, query=..., model=...):
    try:
        batch = self.session.search(query, models=[model], limit=SEARCH_PAGE, offset=offset)
        items = [...map to result dicts...]
        if gen != self._search_gen:
            return  # user retyped / changed filter — discard
        self._search_results = self._search_results + items   # NEW list, single atomic rebind
        self._search_offset = offset + SEARCH_PAGE
        self._search_has_more = len(items) == SEARCH_PAGE and self._search_offset < SEARCH_MAX
    finally:
        self._search_loading_more = False
```

Crucial no-locks detail: rebind a fresh list (`old + items`) rather than `.extend()` — the 4fps render loop iterating `self._search_results[page_start:page_end]` then always sees a consistent snapshot. Footer while more pages exist: `Page N (X results, ↓ for more…)`; while fetching: a dim `loading more…` line. The existing `Page N/M` math needs no change since it derives from `len(_search_results)`.

Backspace/typing branches also bump `_search_gen` (they already clear results), which invalidates any in-flight page fetch.

## 3. Search WITHIN my playlists (client-side index)

New module `src/ticli/utils/playlist_index.py`, mirroring `credential_store.py`'s module-function style (no class, chmod-600 file, swallow-and-log errors):

- `INDEX_FILE = Path.home() / ".config" / "ticli" / "playlist_index.json"` (dir mode 0o700, file 0o600 — same as `STATE_FILE` handling in `_save_state`).
- Schema:
```json
{"version": 1, "built_at": 1753370000.0,
 "playlists": {"<uuid>": {"name": "...", "last_updated": "ISO-or-null", "num_tracks": 42,
   "tracks": [{"id": 123, "name": "...", "artist": "...", "album": "...", "duration": 213, "pos": 0}]}}}
```
- `load_index() -> Optional[dict]` / `save_index(index)` — trivial JSON round-trip.
- `refresh_index(session, cached, on_progress) -> dict`: calls `session.user.playlists()`; for each playlist, skip refetch when the cached entry matches both `pl.last_updated.isoformat()` and `pl.num_tracks` (if `last_updated is None`, compare `num_tracks` only — still catches add/remove); else page `pl.tracks(limit=100, offset=o)` until short page. Drops cached playlists no longer returned. Calls `on_progress(i, total, name)` per playlist so the TUI shows "Indexing 4/12: Gym Mix…". First build for ~30 playlists ≈ 30–60 requests, then incremental refreshes are ~1 request total when nothing changed.
- `search_index(index, query, limit=200) -> list[dict]`: case-insensitive substring match on `f"{name} {artist} {album}"`, name-prefix matches ranked first; each hit is `{"type": "mytrack", "name", "artist", "playlist_name", "playlist_id", "track_id", "pos"}`.

Player-side state: `_my_index: Optional[dict] = None`, `_index_building = False`, `_index_status = ""`. `_rebuild_playlist_index(force=False)` runs `refresh_index` in a daemon thread (loading disk cache first via `load_index()`); on completion it saves, sets `_my_index`, and — if still `filter == "mine"` with an unchanged `_search_gen` — re-runs the query so results appear without another Enter.

**Freshness story**: (a) entering the `mine` filter loads the disk cache instantly and searches it, then kicks a background incremental refresh if `time.time() - built_at > 900` (15 min TTL) or no cache; (b) Ctrl-R forces a full rebuild; (c) results header shows dim `index: 12 playlists · updated 3m ago` plus `_index_status` while building. Search never blocks on the network — stale results now, corrected results when the refresh lands.

**Selecting a `mytrack` result**: `_select_search_result` gains a branch calling new `_open_playlist_at(playlist_id, pos, title)`: `_push_nav()`, enter MODE_BROWSE loading state, daemon thread does `pl = self.session.playlist(playlist_id)` then `pl.tracks()` pagination into `_browse_tracks`, finally `_browse_cursor = min(pos, len-1)`. So Enter lands you *inside the playlist positioned on the match*, and the existing browse Enter (`_play_browse_track`) plays it with the whole playlist as the queue — the natural behavior, zero new playback code.

Display for `mine` rows: `[MY] Track Name  Artist  in «Playlist Name»` (playlist name dim); reuses the existing search row renderer with one extra dim segment when `item.get("playlist_name")`.

## Threading summary
All network work stays on daemon threads mutating shared state (existing pattern); the new `_search_gen` counter + whole-list rebinds are the only concurrency additions. Index refresh writes the JSON file only from its single worker thread; only one refresh runs at a time (`_index_building` guard).

## Ship order (each piece independently mergeable)
1. Filter bar + Tab/Shift-Tab + playlists-as-a-search-type (~80 LOC).
2. Infinite scroll on single-type filters (~50 LOC).
3. `playlist_index.py` + `mine` filter + Ctrl-R + `_open_playlist_at` (~200 LOC).

designs.summary: Close the gap between what _save_state already persists (queue IDs, queue index, position) and what _restore_state actually uses (queue + index only — position is written but never read). On launch, restore the queue and current track by ID, set the player view to paused-at-saved-position, and make space-to-play fetch a fresh stream URL and start ffplay with -ss at that offset. No autoplay. Add crash-safe periodic + on-transition state saves with atomic writes, and explicit failure paths for unstreamable tracks, offline launch, and old/mismatched state files.
designs.approach:
## What works today vs what's missing (exact audit of player.py)

**Works today:**
- `_save_state()` (player.py:408) writes `track_ids`, `queue_index`, `position` (from `_get_position()`), `search_history` to `~/.config/ticli/player_state.json` (0600). It is called exactly once, in the `finally` block of `run()` (player.py:1432) — i.e. **on quit only** (clean quit or Ctrl+C, since KeyboardInterrupt reaches the finally). SIGTERM, crash, or terminal window close loses everything. The write is `write_text` — not atomic, so a crash mid-write can leave torn JSON (which `_restore_state` then silently discards).
- `_restore_state()` (player.py:423) restores `search_history` synchronously, then a daemon thread re-fetches each track ID via `self.session.track(tid)` (one HTTP request per track, sequential), and on success sets `self._queue`, `self._queue_index`, `self._current_track`. So the track name/artist/duration DO reappear in the player view after a few seconds.

**Missing / broken:**
1. **Position is saved but never read.** `data["position"]` is dead data — the restored track always shows 0:00 and space plays from the beginning.
2. **Space-to-play ignores any position anyway.** `_toggle_play()` (player.py:485) with a restored track hits the `elif self._current_track:` branch → `_play_track(track)` → `audio.play_url(url)` with `seek=0` and resets `_play_offset = 0`.
3. **`_play_track()` has no seek parameter**, even though `AudioPlayer.play_url(url, seek=...)` already accepts one.
4. **`play_url` seek path is broken for fresh plays** (player.py:131): `source = url if seek == 0 else self._cache_file` — but `play_url` just spawned the ffmpeg cache download milliseconds earlier, so on any fresh call with seek>0 the cache file is empty/partial. This also affects the existing `resume()` cache-miss fallback.
5. **Wrong-track restore when queue shrinks.** Restore skips tracks that fail to fetch, then does `idx = min(queue_index, len(tracks)-1)` — if a track *before* the current one was removed from TIDAL, the index points at the wrong track. The current track's identity (its ID) is never saved.
6. **Restore clobber race.** If the user searches and plays something in the first seconds after launch, the restore thread finishes and overwrites `_queue`/`_queue_index`/`_current_track` — display then shows a different track than what's audible.
7. **Offline launch destroys state.** Network down → every `session.track()` call fails → nothing restored → on quit `_save_state()` writes the now-empty queue, wiping the previous session.
8. **Stream URL staleness: non-issue by design, keep it that way.** URLs are never persisted; `Track.get_url()` (tidalapi media.py:410, `tracks/%s/urlpostpaywall`) returns a short-lived signed CDN URL and is called at play time. The resume design must keep fetching the URL lazily at space-press, never at restore time and never from disk.
9. **Quality mismatch: mostly a non-issue.** Track IDs and position-in-seconds are quality-agnostic; `session.audio_quality` only affects `get_url()` at play time. A state file saved under LOSSLESS resumed under HIRES just streams the new quality from the same timestamp. Save `quality` in the file for diagnostics but do not invalidate on mismatch.

## Design

### State schema v2 (`~/.config/ticli/player_state.json`)
```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "track_ids": [401293, ...],
  "current_track_id": 401293,
  "queue_index": 3,
  "position": 142.7,
  "quality": "LOSSLESS",
  "saved_at": 1753380000.0,
  "search_history": ["..."]
}
```
`current_track_id` is authoritative for locating the current track after filtering; `queue_index` is kept as fallback for v1 files (no `version` key → treat as v1, current behavior). `quality` mirrors the label already computed in `_build_player_display` (player.py:616). New instance attributes: `_player_message: str = ""`, `_restore_snapshot: Optional[dict] = None`, `_restore_done: bool = False`, `_last_state_save: float = 0`.

### Restore flow (`_restore_state` rework)
1. Synchronous part unchanged (search history) plus: stash the parsed dict in `self._restore_snapshot`, clamp `position = max(0.0, float(data.get("position", 0)))`.
2. Daemon thread, **two-phase fetch** for perceived speed:
   - Phase 1: fetch only `current_track_id` via `session.track(tid)` (1 request). On success, commit immediately: `_current_track = t`, `_queue = [t]`, `_queue_index = 0`, `_play_offset = min(position, max(0, (t.duration or 0) - 1))`, `_playing = False`, `_play_start_time = None`, `_player_message = "Restored last session — space to resume"`. The existing `_build_player_display` already renders paused-at-position for free: `_get_position()` returns `_play_offset` when not playing, the ⏸ icon comes from `_playing = False`, and the progress bar fills from `position/duration`. No display changes needed beyond one `_player_message` line.
   - Phase 2: fetch the remaining IDs in saved order; per-track `except ObjectNotFound: continue` (dropped from queue); on completion rebuild `_queue` with the phase-1 track object spliced at its saved slot and recompute `_queue_index = next(i for i,t in enumerate(queue) if t.id == current_track_id)`. Set `_restore_done = True`.
3. **Clobber guard:** before each commit, check `if self._current_track is not None and self._current_track.id != current_track_id: return` (user already started something → abandon restore silently, set `_restore_done = True` so saves proceed normally). Same GIL-atomic-assignment threading model as the rest of the file; no locks, tiny benign race window, consistent with existing code.
4. **Failure classification:** `except tidalapi.exceptions.ObjectNotFound` on phase 1 → current track gone: proceed to phase 2, land on the nearest surviving neighbor (same index position, clamped) with position discarded (0:00) and `_player_message = "Last track no longer available"`. Any other exception (requests ConnectionError, timeout, auth) → abort entirely, keep `_restore_snapshot`, `_restore_done = False`, `_player_message = "Offline — couldn't restore last session"`.

### Resume playback
- `_play_track(self, track, seek: float = 0.0)`: call `self.audio.play_url(url, seek=seek)`, set `self._play_offset = seek` (not 0), clear `_player_message`. Wrap the `track.get_url()` call in `except (URLNotAvailable, StreamNotAvailable, ObjectNotFound)` (all verified in tidalapi/exceptions.py) → `_playing = False`, `_player_message = "Track unavailable — → to skip"` instead of today's silent bare `except`.
- `_toggle_play()` final branch becomes `self._play_track(self._current_track, seek=self._play_offset)`. This is the whole space-to-play resume: URL fetched fresh at keypress (staleness impossible), ffplay started with `-ss <offset>`.
- `AudioPlayer.play_url` ffplay branch fix: `source = url` always (delete the `else self._cache_file` half of line 131) — the cache is never ready at fresh-play time. The ffmpeg cache download still rips the full file from 0, so `_seek_offset` stays an absolute timeline offset and the existing pause (`kill + accumulate elapsed`) / resume (`_play_from_cache(self._seek_offset)`) machinery works unchanged with a nonzero initial seek. This incidentally fixes the pre-existing `resume()` cache-miss fallback too.
- `_build_player_display`: append one dim line after `status_line` when `self._player_message` is set.

### When state is saved (new policy)
1. **On quit** — unchanged (run() finally, player.py:1432).
2. **On track transition** — call `self._save_state()` at the end of a successful `_play_track` (tiny JSON write; `_play_track` already does blocking network on the keypress thread so this adds nothing noticeable).
3. **Periodic while playing** — in the existing `_monitor_playback` loop (player.py:536): `if self._playing and time.time() - self._last_state_save > 30: self._save_state()`. 30s bounds position loss on crash; no writes while paused/idle.
4. **Atomic writes** — `tmp = STATE_FILE.with_suffix(".tmp"); tmp.write_text(json); os.chmod(tmp, 0o600); os.replace(tmp, STATE_FILE)` so a crash never leaves torn JSON (mirrors the defensive style of credential_store.py).
5. **Offline preservation** — in `_save_state`, if `not self._queue and self._restore_snapshot and not self._restore_done`, write the snapshot back verbatim instead of the empty live state. A failed restore must not destroy the previous session.

### Autoplay decision
Recommend **no autoplay** (paused-at-position, space to play): it matches current behavior, avoids surprise audio, and — decisively — avoids a blocking `get_url()` network call during startup before the TUI is even up, plus the unstreamable-track error path happens at an explicit user action where the message is visible. Option noted: a later `--resume-play` flag on cli.py's `@click.option`s could call `_toggle_play()` once `_restore_done` flips true; trivial to add on top of this design.

### Shippable increments (in order)
1. **PR 1 — position resume:** schema v2 write, `_restore_state` two-phase rework with clobber guard, `_play_track(seek=)`, `_toggle_play` change, `play_url` source fix. This alone delivers the headline feature.
2. **PR 2 — crash-safe saves:** atomic write, save-on-transition, 30s periodic save in `_monitor_playback`.
3. **PR 3 — failure polish:** `_player_message` UI line, ObjectNotFound/URLNotAvailable handling, offline snapshot preservation.

### Testing
Existing test style is CLI-level, but `_save_state`/`_restore_state` logic (schema v2 round-trip, v1 fallback, current_track_id relocation after dropped tracks, offline snapshot preservation) is testable with a stubbed `session.track` and tmp_path-patched `STATE_FILE` — no TIDAL needed, matching the "no running TIDAL instance" test constraint.

Persisting the stream URL to skip the space-press fetch: rejected — urlpostpaywall URLs are short-lived signed CDN links, so a stored URL is stale within minutes-to-hours and would add a broken-URL failure path for zero real benefit. Persisting the ffmpeg cache file (/tmp/ticli-cache-*.flac) across sessions for instant offline resume: rejected for scope — /tmp is volatile, the file may be partial, and it couples resume to cache lifecycle; fresh-URL-with--ss is simpler and always correct. Invalidating the state file on quality mismatch: rejected — track IDs and second-based positions are quality-agnostic, so mismatch is harmless; the quality key is stored for diagnostics only. Adding a threading.Lock around queue state: rejected for this feature — the file deliberately runs lock-free with GIL-atomic assignments, and introducing partial locking piecemeal would give false confidence; the clobber guard covers the one new observable race.

designs.summary: Add a spec-driven settings module (`src/ticli/utils/config.py`) that persists user preferences to a new `~/.config/ticli/config.json` (kept separate from `player_state.json`, which stays ephemeral session state), plus a new `MODE_SETTINGS` TUI page opened with `g` from player mode. A single `SETTINGS_SPEC` table (key, label, kind, bounds/choices, description) drives defaults, load-time validation, the settings list rendering, and the edit UX (Left/Right cycle-or-step, Enter toggle/commit, digit keys for direct numeric entry) — so future features (artwork, caching, resume) add one spec row and call `self.config[...]`.
designs.approach:
## 1. Where preferences live: new `config.json`, not `player_state.json`

Recommend a **separate `~/.config/ticli/config.json`**. Reasons:
- `player_state.json` is rewritten wholesale on every exit by `_save_state()` (player.py:408-421) with a fixed dict — preferences mixed in would be clobbered unless `_save_state` round-trips them, coupling two unrelated lifecycles.
- State is machine-owned and disposable (delete it, lose your queue); config is user-owned, hand-editable, and should survive a state reset.
- Write timing differs: state saves once at exit; config saves write-through on each edit so a crash never loses a setting.

Both files live in the existing `STATE_DIR` (`~/.config/ticli/`, already created 0o700).

## 2. `src/ticli/utils/config.py` (new, ~120 LOC, styled after credential_store.py)

Module-level constants + plain functions, `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`, swallow-and-log I/O errors, no new deps (stdlib json/pathlib only — no keyring; config is not secret).

```python
CONFIG_DIR = Path.home() / ".config" / "ticli"
CONFIG_FILE = CONFIG_DIR / "config.json"

PAGE_SIZE_AUTO = 0  # sentinel: fit to terminal height

SETTINGS_SPEC: list[dict] = [
    {"key": "page_size",  "label": "List length",      "kind": "int",
     "default": PAGE_SIZE_AUTO, "min": 0, "max": 40, "step": 1,
     "render_zero_as": "auto",
     "desc": "Rows per list page. 0 = auto-fit to terminal height."},
    {"key": "quality",    "label": "Default quality",  "kind": "choice",
     "default": "HIGH", "choices": ["LOW", "HIGH", "LOSSLESS", "HIRES"],
     "desc": "Startup audio quality. --quality flag overrides for one run. Applies from next track."},
    {"key": "artwork",    "label": "Album artwork",    "kind": "bool",
     "default": False,
     "desc": "Show album art in the player (terminal image support required)."},
    # room to grow — one row each when the features land:
    # {"key": "autoplay_on_launch", "kind": "bool", "default": False, ...}
    # {"key": "cache_max_mb",      "kind": "int",  "default": 100, ...}
]
DEFAULTS = {s["key"]: s["default"] for s in SETTINGS_SPEC}

def load_config() -> dict        # DEFAULTS | file contents, each value passed through _coerce()
def save_config(cfg: dict) -> None   # json.dumps(known keys only), mkdir 0o700, no chmod needed (not secret) — but keep 0o600 for consistency with STATE_FILE
def _coerce(spec, value)         # typed validation: int→clamp to [min,max] (ValueError→default);
                                 # choice→uppercase, must be in choices else default;
                                 # bool→bool(value)
def get_spec(key) -> dict        # lookup helper for the UI
```

`_coerce` is the "typed accessor": callers get guaranteed-valid values out of `load_config()`, so `self.config["page_size"]` is always a clamped int — no defensive code at call sites. Unknown keys in the file are dropped on load (and thus on next save), keeping the file canonical.

## 3. Data flow / threading

- `HeadlessTidalPlayer.__init__` gains `self.config = load_config()` and `self._settings_cursor = 0`, `self._settings_entry: Optional[str] = None` (numeric entry buffer).
- **`self.config` is mutated only on the main thread** (the key-handling/render loop in `run()` is single-threaded — `_handle_key` and `_build_display` alternate in the same `while self.running` loop, player.py:1421-1428). Daemon threads may *read* config (e.g. future artwork fetcher) — same benign-race model as today's shared state; no locks added.
- Every committed edit calls `save_config(self.config)` synchronously. It is a <1 KB JSON write; at 4 fps on the main thread this is imperceptible and guarantees crash-safety.

## 4. Setting semantics

### page_size → dynamic list heights
Today `PAGE_SIZE = 15` (player.py:60) is used **only inside the four list display builders** for pagination math (`page_start = (cursor // PAGE_SIZE) * PAGE_SIZE`, `page_end`, page-count footer): `_build_search_display` (:658-676), `_build_browse_display` (:695-724), `_build_queue_display` (:736-765), `_build_playlists_display` (:779-802). Cursor movement is ±1 and never references PAGE_SIZE, so page size can change between frames (setting edited, terminal resized) and pagination simply recomputes — no state invalidation needed.

Replace all PAGE_SIZE reads in those four builders with a new method:

```python
def _page_size(self) -> int:
    CHROME_ROWS = 16  # panel borders(2) + padding(2) + player block(4) + separator(3)
                      # + list header(1) + page footer(2) + controls(2)
    fit = self.console.size.height - CHROME_ROWS   # rich.Console.size → ConsoleDimensions (verified)
    configured = self.config["page_size"]
    if configured == PAGE_SIZE_AUTO:
        return max(3, fit)
    return max(3, min(configured, fit))            # never overflow the terminal
```

Called once at the top of each builder (`page = self._page_size()`), so all four lists stay consistent within a frame. Default changes from fixed-15 to auto-fit; a user who wants the old behavior sets `page_size: 15`. Delete the `PAGE_SIZE` module constant (grep confirms no other users).

### quality → config default, `--quality` becomes an override
- `cli.py`: change `@click.option("--quality", default="HIGH", ...)` to `default=None` (keep the same `click.Choice`), help text "Audio quality (overrides configured default for this run)". Same change in the legacy `main()` inside player.py (:1443).
- `HeadlessTidalPlayer.__init__(self, quality: Optional[str] = None)`: load config first, then `quality = (quality or self.config["quality"]).upper()` before the existing `quality_map` lookup (:312-318). Store the map as a class-level `QUALITY_MAP` so the settings handler reuses it.
- Editing quality in the settings page applies live: `self.session.audio_quality = QUALITY_MAP[new_value]`. Verified in installed tidalapi 0.8.x: `Session.audio_quality` is a property writing `session.config.quality` (session.py:756-761), and `Track.get_url()` sends `"audioquality": self.session.config.quality` per request (media.py:419-424, 510) — so the change takes effect on the **next** `_play_track()` without restart. The settings row description says "applies from next track". The player-mode quality badge (:616-622) already reads `self.session.audio_quality`, so it updates automatically.

### artwork → stored + toggleable now, consumed later
Plain bool row. The artwork feature reads `self.config["artwork"]` each frame; until it ships the toggle persists harmlessly. No coupling needed here beyond the spec row.

## 5. MODE_SETTINGS UI

### Entry keybinding
`MODE_SETTINGS = "settings"` class constant next to the others (:257-261). Open with **`g`** from player mode (mnemonic "gear"; `s/t/m/l/r/q/p/o/n/k` are taken, `g` is free). In `_handle_player_key` add:

```python
elif key == "g":
    self._mini_player = False
    self._mode = self.MODE_SETTINGS
    self._settings_cursor = 0
    self._settings_entry = None
    self._nav_history.clear()
```

Advertise it in the `_show_more` block of the controls footer (`[g] settings`, alongside `[o] logout`). Settings is a top-level page like queue/playlists: Esc returns straight to `MODE_PLAYER`, no `_push_nav()` entry (matches `_handle_queue_key`/`_handle_playlists_key` behavior at :1316-1317, :1338-1339).

### `_handle_settings_key(self, key)` — dispatched from `_handle_key` (:1204-1213)
Editing model chosen for cbreak + escape-sequence input: **no modal "edit mode" for toggles/choices — Left/Right adjust in place**. This deviates from Left=back used elsewhere; in settings, Left/Right-to-adjust is the universal TUI convention and Esc remains back. Space still toggles play/pause (consistency with every other list mode, reusing the `_space_held` guard).

```
Esc            → if _settings_entry is not None: cancel entry; else MODE_PLAYER
Up/Down        → move _settings_cursor (clamped 0..len(SETTINGS_SPEC)-1); cancels any entry
Right / Enter  → bool: toggle;  choice: cycle forward;  int: +step (Enter commits entry if buffer active)
Left           → bool: toggle;  choice: cycle backward; int: -step
digits 0-9     → int rows only: start/extend _settings_entry buffer (max 3 chars)
Backspace      → shrink entry buffer
Space          → play/pause (guarded by _space_held, like _handle_queue_key :1319-1324)
```

Commit path (one helper `_apply_setting(key, value)`): coerce via `config._coerce(spec, value)` (clamps out-of-range numeric entry instead of rejecting), assign into `self.config`, `save_config(self.config)`, then per-key side effects — currently only `quality` → set `self.session.audio_quality`. `page_size`/`artwork` need no side effect because they are read live each frame.

### `_build_settings_display() -> Text` — same shape as `_build_playlists_display`

```
   Settings
                                          ← blank line
   ▸ List length      ‹ auto ›            ← cursor row: bold white label, cyan ‹value›
     Default quality    HIGH
     Album artwork      off               ← bools render on/off (green/dim)
                                          
   Rows per list page. 0 = auto-fit to terminal height.   ← dim desc of selected row
```

- Cursor marker `  ▸ ` in bold cyan, exactly like the other lists (:786-789).
- Selected row's value gets `‹ ›` chevrons signalling Left/Right adjusts it.
- Int row with active entry buffer renders `List length   23█` reusing the search-input block-cursor idiom (:648-650).
- Description line comes from `spec["desc"]` — self-documenting as settings are added.
- No pagination needed (<10 settings for the foreseeable future); trivially reuses `_page_size()` later if the list grows.

Wire into `_build_display`: add `MODE_SETTINGS` branches in the mode content section (:918-925) and the controls footer section (:856-898) — footer: `[↑/↓] select  [←/→] change  [0-9] type  [Space] pause/play  [Esc] back`. At 4 fps every edit is visible within 250 ms, same latency as all existing interactions; no extra refresh handling required.

## 6. Tests (`src/ticli/tests/test_config.py`)
Pure-unit, no TIDAL, matching existing no-network test philosophy:
- defaults returned when file missing; unknown keys dropped; corrupt JSON → defaults (no crash)
- `_coerce`: int clamping ("999"→40, -5→0/min), bad choice → default, case-insensitive choice
- round-trip save/load (monkeypatch `config.CONFIG_FILE` to tmp_path)
- CLI: `--quality` omitted → `HeadlessTidalPlayer` receives None (CliRunner, mock the player class)

## 7. Incremental shipping plan (three small PRs)
1. **PR 1 — infrastructure, no UI**: `utils/config.py` + tests; `_page_size()` wired into the four builders; `--quality` fallback in cli.py/player.py. Immediately useful: hand-edit config.json to change list length/quality.
2. **PR 2 — the page**: `MODE_SETTINGS`, `_handle_settings_key`, `_build_settings_display`, `g` binding, `_build_display` branches. Left/Right + Enter editing only.
3. **PR 3 — polish**: digit direct-entry buffer, `‹ ›` chevrons/desc line styling, artwork/autoplay rows as the owning features land.

NEW: unit tests for defaults/merge/coercion/clamping/corrupt-file handling with monkeypatched CONFIG_FILE, plus CliRunner test that omitted --quality passes None through.

risks: CHROME_ROWS estimate (16) may be off by a row or two depending on mode (search shows a query line, browse shows Play All), causing the panel to slightly overflow small terminals in auto mode — mitigate by measuring per-mode during PR 1 and keeping the max(3, ...) floor.

Left/Right meaning 'adjust value' in settings conflicts with Left='back' in every other mode; users may reflexively press Left expecting to exit and instead toggle a setting. Footer hint and Esc-only-back mitigate; worst case is one benign, immediately visible toggle.
Changing default page_size from fixed 15 to auto-fit changes existing look on tall terminals; users may be surprised by longer lists (set page_size: 15 to restore).
Runtime quality change only affects the next get_url() call — the currently playing track keeps its stream; users may think the setting 'didn't work' (desc line says 'applies from next track').

Two writers to ~/.config/ticli: config.json (config.py) and player_state.json (_save_state). Keys must not migrate between them silently; SETTINGS_SPEC is the single source of truth for what belongs in config.

Numeric entry buffer adds a third input micro-mode (after search text and confirmations); Esc now has context-dependent meaning inside settings (cancel entry vs leave page) — kept unambiguous by rendering the block cursor whenever a buffer is active.
open_questions: Keybinding: is 'g' (gear) acceptable, or would you prefer ',' (desktop-app convention, Cmd+,) or 'c' (config)? All three are currently unbound in player mode.
Should page_size default to auto-fit (0) as designed, or keep 15 as the default and make auto opt-in — i.e., preserve today's exact look for existing users?

When quality is changed in settings while a track is playing, should ticli restart the current track at the new quality (costs a re-buffer + loses the ffplay cache) or only apply to the next track (designed behavior)?
Should the artwork row be hidden until the artwork feature ships, or shown now as a persisted-but-inert toggle (designed behavior: shown, so the settings page has 3 rows on day one)?
